heading: Honest Words, Fair Play
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Basic Manners – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 10–13.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Basic Manners (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: People {trust|trust} friends who tell the truth. Imagine you ate the last piece of pie that your mum was saving for your dad. It might be {tempting|tempting} to blame the dog, but {owning up|owning up} is always the better choice. The same is true if you made a silly face at your baby sister and made her cry. Admitting what you did shows that you are honest, and {honesty|honesty} builds trust.

paras.label: B
paras.text: However, being honest does not mean saying every thought that comes into your head. Some comments can hurt people's feelings, especially comments about how someone looks or smells. Nobody wants to be called "stinky feet", even if their feet really do smell! In situations like this, the kindest thing is to keep your thoughts to yourself.

paras.label: C
paras.text: Games are another place where manners matter. Whether you win or lose, you should behave politely when the game is over. Winners should not {brag|brag} or {show off|show off}, and losers should not {sulk|sulk} or get angry. Throwing the cards across the room will not change the result; it will only make others unwilling to play with you next time.

paras.label: D
paras.text: {A good sport|a good sport} accepts that not everyone can win at the same time. Shaking hands or saying "Good game!" to the other players can be hard, especially after a close match, but it shows {maturity|maturity} and respect.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Sadly, even famous players and coaches sometimes lose their temper. You may see your sports hero {throw a fit|throw a fit} or start a fight on TV. Remember that being talented is not the same as being a good {role model|role model}.

vocab.vi: hấp dẫn, dễ khiến mình muốn làm
người chơi đẹp, biết thắng thua

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that explains how admitting a mistake builds trust
items.why: Đoạn A: *Admitting what you did… honesty builds trust.*

items.label: A paragraph that gives an example of a comment that can hurt
items.why: Đoạn B nhắc ví dụ gọi người khác là *"stinky feet"*.

items.label: A paragraph that suggests something to say at the end of a match
items.why: Đoạn D: nói *"Good game!"* với đối thủ.

items.label: A paragraph that says some well-known people do not behave well
items.why: Đoạn E: *even famous players and coaches sometimes lose their temper.*

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest you should do if you ate the pie?
options: Say nothing and hope nobody notices.
questions.why: Đoạn A: *owning up is always the better choice* (nhận lỗi là tốt nhất).

questions.q: The writer believes you should always say exactly what you think.
questions.why: Sai. Đoạn B: trung thực **không có nghĩa** là nói mọi suy nghĩ ra miệng.

questions.q: Why shouldn't you call someone "stinky feet", even if it is true?
options: It is not a funny joke.
They might call you a name too.
questions.why: Đoạn B: lời nhận xét về ngoại hình, mùi cơ thể *can hurt people's feelings*.

questions.q: According to paragraph C, what may happen if you throw the cards across the room?
options: Other people may not want to play with you again.
You may win the next game.
The result of the game will change.
The teacher will give you more cards.
questions.why: *…it will only make others unwilling to play with you next time.*

questions.q: The writer says that saying "Good game!" after a close match is always easy.
questions.why: Sai. Đoạn D: *can be hard, especially after a close match*.

questions.q: What is the main point of paragraph E?
options: Being a famous player doesn't make someone a good example.
You should never watch sport on TV.
Coaches are usually better role models than players.
Talented people never lose their temper.
questions.why: *being talented is not the same as being a good role model.*

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: The girl may be telling the truth. So what is wrong with what she says?
questions.why: Có thể đúng sự thật, nhưng lời nói đó làm người khác tổn thương (đoạn B).
questions.alt: A girl holding her nose and saying Hey, stinky feet!

questions.q: According to the text, what would have been the kindest thing for the girl to do?
options: Take a photo of his boots.
questions.why: Đoạn B: *the kindest thing is to keep your thoughts to yourself.*
questions.alt: A girl holding her nose and saying Hey, stinky feet!

questions.q: Which phrase from the text best describes these two players?
options: role models who throw a fit
questions.why: Hai đội đập tay và nói *Good game!*, đúng tinh thần **a good sport** (đoạn D).
questions.alt: Two football players from different teams giving a high five and saying Good game!

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Last Saturday, our team lost the final by one goal. [1] Our captain, Huy, walked over to the other team and shook their hands. [2] Later, the coach told us she was prouder of us that day than when we won. [3]
options: Some of us wanted to kick the ball away and go straight home.
"Good game," he said, even though he looked disappointed.
She said that losing well is a skill, just like scoring goals.
He told the winners that they had only been lucky.
Then we all threw our water bottles at the referee.

items.why: Sau khi thua, cảm xúc tự nhiên là muốn bỏ về; câu sau *Our captain…* đối lập với cảm xúc đó.
Huy bắt tay và nói *Good game* – đúng với hành động trước đó.
Giải thích lý do huấn luyện viên tự hào: thua đẹp cũng là một kỹ năng.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *…owning up is always the better choice* (A). What does **own up** mean?
options: admit that you did something wrong

questions.q: *…losers should not sulk or get angry* (C). If you **sulk**, you…
options: stay quiet and unhappy because you didn't get what you wanted
questions.why: **Sulk** = hờn dỗi, im lặng tỏ ra không vui.

questions.q: *Winners should not brag* (C). Which word is closest in meaning to **brag**?
*…your sports hero throw a fit* (E). What does **throw a fit** mean?
options: suddenly become very angry and upset
questions.why: **Throw a fit** = nổi cơn tam bành, không phải ném gì.
